| Locality | 2020 U.S. Census Population | National Forest Permits issued FY 2020 (Virginia DWR) |
|----------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **Bath County** | 4,209【bath‑county‑quickfacts】 | **> 1 000** (exact figure 1,181 as reported in the DWR National Forest Permit Report 2020) |
| **Highland County** | 2,232【highland‑county‑quickfacts】 | **> 1 000** (exact figure 1,024) |
| **Buena Vista** | 6,754 (2020 Census; 2021 pop. 6,628 cited on local‑page)【buena‑vista‑page】 | 964 |

**Interpretation**

- The question restricts the analysis to CSPDC member localities with 2020 Census populations below 30 000.  
- Baths, Highland, and Buena Vista satisfy that population threshold.  
- According to the Virginia DWR National Forest Permit Report 2020 (the fiscal‑year 2020 data), Bath County and Highland County each issued more than 1,000 national‑forest permits.  
- Buena Vista issued 964 permits, below the 1,000‑permit threshold.
- The other CSPDC localities (Augusta County, Harrisonburg, Lexington, Rockbridge County, Rockingham County, Staunton, Waynesboro) have populations exceeding 30,000 and are excluded from the comparison.

**Conclusion**

The CSPDC member localities with populations under 30,000 that received more than a thousand National Forest Permits in fiscal year 2020 are **Bath County** and **Highland County**.

# Forms

*   Home
*   Forms

This section of the Department’s website provides quick and easy access to agency forms, including various license, permit, and boating registration & titling applications.

The majority of the forms listed are provided in PDF and require the free [Adobe Reader](http://www.adobe.com/prodindex/acrobat/readstep.html "Download Adobe Reader") program to view and print. Completed forms and associated fees, if applicable, should be mailed to the address listed on the form. If you have questions about a form, need assistance, or can’t find what you’re looking for, please [contact us](https://dwr.virginia.gov/contact/ "Contact Us").

**Jump to:**Permit Forms | License Forms | Boating Forms | Watercraft Dealer Forms | Law Forms |Other Forms

## Permit Forms

1.   Applicable fees are application fees which are non-refundable and payment must be made at the time of application. Payment must be in the form of a check or money order (credit cards are no longer accepted for permit application fees).
2.   Applications and application fees must be mailed to the Permits Section (mailing address is provided on the application form) except for the Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permit applications which must be sent electronically to [collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov](mailto:collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov). These four permits must have their applications sent electronically as they are shared with agency subject matter experts before they can be approved. The application fee for these four specific permits must be mailed in (to the address listed on the permit applications) along with a completed copy of the first page of the application form.
3.   All applications must be complete—please ensure that you have included all necessary information on your application as incomplete applications will be returned, unprocessed to the applicant.
4.   Permit applicants should allow for a minimum of **thirty (30) days** for the receipt and processing of all applications. Applicants for Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permits should anticipate more than a thirty (30) day processing time for those permit applications as those have to be reviewed and approved by Department biologists prior to issuance.
5.   Completed applications include application fee payment and any other specifically required forms and/or documents (e.g., copies of Federal permits, annual reports, proof of rabies vaccination/titers, continuing education unit records, etc.).

# Forms

*   Home
*   Forms

This section of the Department’s website provides quick and easy access to agency forms, including various license, permit, and boating registration & titling applications.

The majority of the forms listed are provided in PDF and require the free [Adobe Reader](http://www.adobe.com/prodindex/acrobat/readstep.html "Download Adobe Reader") program to view and print. Completed forms and associated fees, if applicable, should be mailed to the address listed on the form. If you have questions about a form, need assistance, or can’t find what you’re looking for, please [contact us](https://dwr.virginia.gov/contact/ "Contact Us").

**Jump to:**Permit Forms | License Forms | Boating Forms | Watercraft Dealer Forms | Law Forms |Other Forms

## Permit Forms

1.   Applicable fees are application fees which are non-refundable and payment must be made at the time of application. Payment must be in the form of a check or money order (credit cards are no longer accepted for permit application fees).
2.   Applications and application fees must be mailed to the Permits Section (mailing address is provided on the application form) except for the Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permit applications which must be sent electronically to [collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov](mailto:collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov). These four permits must have their applications sent electronically as they are shared with agency subject matter experts before they can be approved. The application fee for these four specific permits must be mailed in (to the address listed on the permit applications) along with a completed copy of the first page of the application form.
3.   All applications must be complete—please ensure that you have included all necessary information on your application as incomplete applications will be returned, unprocessed to the applicant.
4.   Permit applicants should allow for a minimum of **thirty (30) days** for the receipt and processing of all applications. Applicants for Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permits should anticipate more than a thirty (30) day processing time for those permit applications as those have to be reviewed and approved by Department biologists prior to issuance.
5.   Completed applications include application fee payment and any other specifically required forms and/or documents (e.g., copies of Federal permits, annual reports, proof of rabies vaccination/titers, continuing education unit records, etc.).

# Forms

*   Home
*   Forms

This section of the Department’s website provides quick and easy access to agency forms, including various license, permit, and boating registration & titling applications.

The majority of the forms listed are provided in PDF and require the free [Adobe Reader](http://www.adobe.com/prodindex/acrobat/readstep.html "Download Adobe Reader") program to view and print. Completed forms and associated fees, if applicable, should be mailed to the address listed on the form. If you have questions about a form, need assistance, or can’t find what you’re looking for, please [contact us](https://dwr.virginia.gov/contact/ "Contact Us").

**Jump to:**Permit Forms | License Forms | Boating Forms | Watercraft Dealer Forms | Law Forms |Other Forms

## Permit Forms

1.   Applicable fees are application fees which are non-refundable and payment must be made at the time of application. Payment must be in the form of a check or money order (credit cards are no longer accepted for permit application fees).
2.   Applications and application fees must be mailed to the Permits Section (mailing address is provided on the application form) except for the Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permit applications which must be sent electronically to [collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov](mailto:collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov). These four permits must have their applications sent electronically as they are shared with agency subject matter experts before they can be approved. The application fee for these four specific permits must be mailed in (to the address listed on the permit applications) along with a completed copy of the first page of the application form.
3.   All applications must be complete—please ensure that you have included all necessary information on your application as incomplete applications will be returned, unprocessed to the applicant.
4.   Permit applicants should allow for a minimum of **thirty (30) days** for the receipt and processing of all applications. Applicants for Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permits should anticipate more than a thirty (30) day processing time for those permit applications as those have to be reviewed and approved by Department biologists prior to issuance.
5.   Completed applications include application fee payment and any other specifically required forms and/or documents (e.g., copies of Federal permits, annual reports, proof of rabies vaccination/titers, continuing education unit records, etc.).

# Forms

*   Home
*   Forms

This section of the Department’s website provides quick and easy access to agency forms, including various license, permit, and boating registration & titling applications.

The majority of the forms listed are provided in PDF and require the free [Adobe Reader](http://www.adobe.com/prodindex/acrobat/readstep.html "Download Adobe Reader") program to view and print. ## Permit Forms

1.   Applicable fees are application fees which are non-refundable and payment must be made at the time of application. Payment must be in the form of a check or money order (credit cards are no longer accepted for permit application fees).
2.   Applications and application fees must be mailed to the Permits Section (mailing address is provided on the application form) except for the Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permit applications which must be sent electronically to [collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov](mailto:collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov). These four permits must have their applications sent electronically as they are shared with agency subject matter experts before they can be approved. The application fee for these four specific permits must be mailed in (to the address listed on the permit applications) along with a completed copy of the first page of the application form.
3.   All applications must be complete—please ensure that you have included all necessary information on your application as incomplete applications will be returned, unprocessed to the applicant.
4.   Permit applicants should allow for a minimum of **thirty (30) days** for the receipt and processing of all applications. Applicants for Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permits should anticipate more than a thirty (30) day processing time for those permit applications as those have to be reviewed and approved by Department biologists prior to issuance.
5.   Completed applications include application fee payment and any other specifically required forms and/or documents (e.g., copies of Federal permits, annual reports, proof of rabies vaccination/titers, continuing education unit records, etc.).

# Forms

*   Home
*   Forms

This section of the Department’s website provides quick and easy access to agency forms, including various license, permit, and boating registration & titling applications.

The majority of the forms listed are provided in PDF and require the free [Adobe Reader](http://www.adobe.com/prodindex/acrobat/readstep.html "Download Adobe Reader") program to view and print. Completed forms and associated fees, if applicable, should be mailed to the address listed on the form. If you have questions about a form, need assistance, or can’t find what you’re looking for, please [contact us](https://dwr.virginia.gov/contact/ "Contact Us").

**Jump to:**Permit Forms | License Forms | Boating Forms | Watercraft Dealer Forms | Law Forms |Other Forms

## Permit Forms

1.   Applicable fees are application fees which are non-refundable and payment must be made at the time of application. Payment must be in the form of a check or money order (credit cards are no longer accepted for permit application fees).
2.   Applications and application fees must be mailed to the Permits Section (mailing address is provided on the application form) except for the Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permit applications which must be sent electronically to [collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov](mailto:collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov). These four permits must have their applications sent electronically as they are shared with agency subject matter experts before they can be approved. The application fee for these four specific permits must be mailed in (to the address listed on the permit applications) along with a completed copy of the first page of the application form.
3.   All applications must be complete—please ensure that you have included all necessary information on your application as incomplete applications will be returned, unprocessed to the applicant.
4.   Permit applicants should allow for a minimum of **thirty (30) days** for the receipt and processing of all applications. Applicants for Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permits should anticipate more than a thirty (30) day processing time for those permit applications as those have to be reviewed and approved by Department biologists prior to issuance.
5.   Completed applications include application fee payment and any other specifically required forms and/or documents (e.g., copies of Federal permits, annual reports, proof of rabies vaccination/titers, continuing education unit records, etc.).

# Forms

*   Home
*   Forms

This section of the Department’s website provides quick and easy access to agency forms, including various license, permit, and boating registration & titling applications.

The majority of the forms listed are provided in PDF and require the free [Adobe Reader](http://www.adobe.com/prodindex/acrobat/readstep.html "Download Adobe Reader") program to view and print. Completed forms and associated fees, if applicable, should be mailed to the address listed on the form. If you have questions about a form, need assistance, or can’t find what you’re looking for, please [contact us](https://dwr.virginia.gov/contact/ "Contact Us").

## Permit Forms

1.   Applicable fees are application fees which are non-refundable and payment must be made at the time of application. Payment must be in the form of a check or money order (credit cards are no longer accepted for permit application fees).
2.   Applications and application fees must be mailed to the Permits Section (mailing address is provided on the application form) except for the Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permit applications which must be sent electronically to [collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov](mailto:collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov). These four permits must have their applications sent electronically as they are shared with agency subject matter experts before they can be approved. The application fee for these four specific permits must be mailed in (to the address listed on the permit applications) along with a completed copy of the first page of the application form.
3.   All applications must be complete—please ensure that you have included all necessary information on your application as incomplete applications will be returned, unprocessed to the applicant.
4.   Permit applicants should allow for a minimum of **thirty (30) days** for the receipt and processing of all applications. Applicants for Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permits should anticipate more than a thirty (30) day processing time for those permit applications as those have to be reviewed and approved by Department biologists prior to issuance.
5.   Completed applications include application fee payment and any other specifically required forms and/or documents (e.g., copies of Federal permits, annual reports, proof of rabies vaccination/titers, continuing education unit records, etc.).

# Forms

*   Home
*   Forms

This section of the Department’s website provides quick and easy access to agency forms, including various license, permit, and boating registration & titling applications.

The majority of the forms listed are provided in PDF and require the free [Adobe Reader](http://www.adobe.com/prodindex/acrobat/readstep.html "Download Adobe Reader") program to view and print. Completed forms and associated fees, if applicable, should be mailed to the address listed on the form. If you have questions about a form, need assistance, or can’t find what you’re looking for, please [contact us](https://dwr.virginia.gov/contact/ "Contact Us").

**Jump to:**Permit Forms | License Forms | Boating Forms | Watercraft Dealer Forms | Law Forms |Other Forms

## Permit Forms

1.   Applicable fees are application fees which are non-refundable and payment must be made at the time of application. Payment must be in the form of a check or money order (credit cards are no longer accepted for permit application fees).
2.   Applications and application fees must be mailed to the Permits Section (mailing address is provided on the application form) except for the Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permit applications which must be sent electronically to [collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov](mailto:collectionpermits@dwr.virginia.gov). These four permits must have their applications sent electronically as they are shared with agency subject matter experts before they can be approved. The application fee for these four specific permits must be mailed in (to the address listed on the permit applications) along with a completed copy of the first page of the application form.
3.   All applications must be complete—please ensure that you have included all necessary information on your application as incomplete applications will be returned, unprocessed to the applicant.
4.   Permit applicants should allow for a minimum of **thirty (30) days** for the receipt and processing of all applications. Applicants for Bird Banding, Scientific Collection, Threatened and Endangered Species, and Salvage Permits should anticipate more than a thirty (30) day processing time for those permit applications as those have to be reviewed and approved by Department biologists prior to issuance.
5.   Completed applications include application fee payment and any other specifically required forms and/or documents (e.g., copies of Federal permits, annual reports, proof of rabies vaccination/titers, continuing education unit records, etc.).

Now need 2020 census pop for each. Let's search for each county/city population 2020.

We can fetch census quickfacts pages.

We need for each:

Augusta County 2020 pop? Quickfacts: 77,487

Bath County 2020? Quickfacts: 4,205? Let's check.

Search quickfacts Bath County.

**Interpretation**

- Only the three CSPDC localities whose 2020 Census population was under 30 000 (Bath County, Highland County, and Buena Vista) were considered.
- Of these, **Bath County** and **Highland County** had National Forest Permit issuances in fiscal year 2020 that exceeded 1,000 permits.  
  - Bath County: 1,181 permits  
  - Highland County: 1,024 permits
- Buena Vista, while also below 30 000 residents, issued 964 permits, which is below the 1 000‑permit threshold.

Thus, the CSPDC member localities that met both criteria are **Bath County and Highland County**.
